score_rationale: Outstanding willingness-to-pay from four high-value B2B segments: government contractor consultants (GovCon coaches charging $5K–$50K for GSA Schedule application support), subcontractor prospect hunters, teaming agreement brokers, and B2B vendors selling to federal contractors. GSA publishes a free, downloadable Excel file of all GSA Schedule contract holders via GSA eLibrary (gsaelibrary.gsa.gov) with company name, DUNS/UEI, contract number, schedule type (IT 70, Professional Services, Facilities Maintenance, etc.), NAICS codes, and business size (small, veteran-owned, woman-owned, HUBZone, 8(a)). This is the exact data that GovCon intelligence platforms like GovTribe, Bloomberg Government, and Deltek charge $3,000–$15,000/year to access. The buyer population is massive: 30,000+ companies hold active GSA Schedules, creating a target market of 100,000+ subcontractors, teaming partners, and service vendors. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces. Engineering lift is low — direct download from GSA eLibrary, deduplicate, and enrich with NAICS and size fields. Zero PII — all company-level business data. Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from GovCon consultants and subcontractors, clear data availability, and absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all active GSA Schedule contract holders, extracted from the GSA eLibrary database — fully public and downloadable without authentication from gsaelibrary.gsa.gov. Each record includes the company legal name, Unique Entity ID (UEI, formerly DUNS), GSA Schedule contract number, schedule type/category (e.g., IT Schedule 70, Professional Services Schedule, Facilities Maintenance MAS), NAICS codes offered under the schedule, contract period of performance (start and end dates), business size and socioeconomic classifications (small business, veteran-owned, woman-owned, HUBZone, 8(a), service-disabled veteran-owned), primary point of contact (where publicly listed), and company headquarters city and state. As of 2025, approximately 30,000 companies hold active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contracts — representing pre-vetted suppliers eligible to sell to all federal agencies via simplified procurement. Government contractor (GovCon) consulting firms charge $5,000–$50,000 to help companies apply for GSA Schedules, and subcontractor matchmaking platforms like PartnerTap and Winvale charge $200–$500/month for teaming partner databases. A one-time $79 CSV targets GovCon consultants prospecting for GSA application clients, subcontractors seeking prime contractor teaming partners, teaming agreement brokers, and B2B service vendors (payroll, insurance, software, recruiting) selling to federal contractors.

audience.who: Government contracting (GovCon) consultants and proposal writers (RSM Federal, Grant Thornton Public Sector, Censeo Consulting, plus thousands of solo GovCon coaches) who help companies apply for GSA Schedules, SAM.gov registration, and federal contract bidding — they cold-call small businesses selling to federal agencies but lacking GSA Schedules, using the list to identify prospects with federal revenue who need schedule certification to scale; subcontractors and teaming partners building databases of prime contractors with GSA Schedules in complementary NAICS codes (e.g., a cybersecurity subcontractor targeting IT Schedule 70 primes, or a facilities management sub targeting Facilities Maintenance MAS holders); teaming agreement brokers and matchmaking platforms (like PartnerTap, Winvale, and boutique GovCon networking firms) connecting small businesses with large primes for joint ventures, mentor-protégé relationships, and subcontracting opportunities; B2B service vendors targeting federal contractors — payroll providers (ADP, Paychex), professional liability insurers (Hiscox, The Hartford), recruiting agencies, HR software (BambooHR, Rippling), and accounting firms all sell heavily to government contractors, who represent a high-LTV, sticky customer segment; federal sales training and certification course providers (e.g., companies offering GSA Schedules 101, GWAC bidding courses, or SAM.gov registration workshops) marketing to companies that just won their first GSA Schedule and need ongoing education.

data_wanted: GSA eLibrary — free, public database of all GSA Schedule (Multiple Award Schedule / MAS) contract holders, downloadable as Excel or CSV from https://www.gsaelibrary.gsa.gov/. No authentication required. Key fields per contract: GSA contract number (format: GS-XXF-XXXXX or 47QRAA##D####), contractor legal name, Unique Entity ID (UEI, 12-character alphanumeric replacing DUNS as of April 2022), contractor CAGE code, schedule name and SIN (Special Item Number, e.g., '54151S IT Professional Services', '541611 Management Consulting'), NAICS codes authorized under the schedule, contract period of performance (award date, current expiration, option periods), business size (small business flag per FAR 19.001, revenue-based or employee-based depending on NAICS), socioeconomic designations (8(a) Business Development participant, HUBZone certified, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB)), contractor address (street, city, state, ZIP), and primary contract contact (name, phone, email — availability varies by contractor; some redact contact details). Scope to active contracts only (exclude expired, closed, or terminated schedules). Approximately 30,000 active GSA Schedule contracts as of 2025 (note: some companies hold multiple schedules, so unique company count is ~20,000–25,000). Target output: 30,000 rows, one per active contract, with all metadata fields. Data updates weekly and is 100% public domain per FAR 9.105-2(b)(1).

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high LTV justification. (1) GovCon consultants: firms like RSM Federal, Grant Thornton Public Sector, and thousands of solo coaches charge $5,000–$50,000 per GSA Schedule application engagement; a $79 CSV that identifies 30,000 companies already holding schedules (competitors to study) PLUS the ability to cross-reference against SAM.gov to find companies selling federally WITHOUT schedules (ideal prospects) creates immediate business development ROI. A single new client engagement yields 60×–600× return. (2) Subcontractors: small businesses seeking teaming partnerships with GSA Schedule primes routinely pay $200–$500/month for platforms like Winvale and PartnerTap; a $79 one-time CSV of all 30,000 active schedule holders — filterable by NAICS, socioeconomic status, and location — delivers the same core prospect universe for 1/3 the cost of a single month's subscription. (3) Teaming brokers: matchmaking firms connecting primes and subs charge $1,000–$5,000 per successful teaming agreement introduction; a $79 database of all GSA primes is a trivial input cost against a single deal. (4) B2B service vendors: payroll, insurance, HR software, and recruiting firms targeting federal contractors know that GovCon companies have 20%–40% higher LTV than commercial SMBs due to contract stability and compliance-driven spending; paying $79 for a full TAM list of schedule holders (with revenue proxies via contract ceiling values) is negligible against $500–$5,000 annual customer value. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 (GovTribe and BGOV sell only annual subscriptions, not one-time data exports) creates a clear low-price entry opportunity.
